statements.quote: We run a pre-registered experiment paired with abductive analysis (Heckman & Singer, 2017; King et al., 2021), which follows recent examples in strategy research that combine empirical rigor with theoretical discovery (e.g., Pillai et al., 2024). statements.quote: The experiments were pre-registered with the AEA RCT Registry. The key differences between the paper and the pre-registration are: • We pre-registered 336 students based on expected enrollment, excluding two students initially categorized as “partners.” Because these students had similar characteristics and eligibility as the main sample, we later included them, bringing the assigned sample to 338. Of these, 305 participated (including the two additions), and 33 were absent. • An attrition analysis comparing observable characteristics of participants and non-participants shows limited imbalance (Table F.1). Only prior consulting experience differs significantly across groups at the 5% level. Results remained consistent if we excluded the two additions (Table F.2), when controlling for consulting experience (Table F.3) and when additionally controlling for gender and age (Table F.4). • We pre-registered three additional outcomes that are not included in the current analysis: (1) how participants prioritized problems when multiple were identified — participants were asked to identify the root cause of the problems without prioritizing them; (2) whether the set of options were mutually exclusive (binary); and (3) whether the best-chosen option reflected an “exit” or “expand” strategy (binary). These were initially registered as primary outcomes but were not analyzed due to a shift in focus toward more theoretically grounded measures of strategic focus. We report the regression results for (2) and (3) in Table F.5. • We also pre-registered the number of “continue” options as an outcome variable. To maintain focus in the main text on broader patterns of strategic reasoning, we report results for this variable in Appendix D, where we examine whether LLM assistance increases participants’ tendency to maintain the status quo rather than propose substantive change. • The pre-analysis plan describes secondary outcomes, some of which we noted at the time as subject to feasibility. We were indeed not able to obtain peer evaluations of option quality and a binary variable on how detailed the option is. • The pre-analysis plan describes that the alternatives generated by participants would be coded by two independent coders. Instead, the options were coded using a fine-tuned GPT-3.5 Turbo model trained on previously human-coded data due to budget constraints.

statements.quote: Unlike the main experiment, which used a standardized, pre-distributed case, this supplementary study drew on strategic challenges that participants were facing in their own companies. Each team worked on a problem contributed by one of its members, which spanned topics as diverse as competitive repositioning, declining profitability, or market expansion (Table G.1 provides further details). The teams collaboratively progressed through three key stages: problem formulation, alternative generation, and selection, following a similar structure to the main experiment. The group task lasted approximately two hours. Immediately after the group task, participants completed an individual online survey capturing their reflections on the team process and their perceptions of the LLM’s contribution.
statements.locator: PDF p. 112 (printed appendix p. 69), Appendix G, team challenges in Table G.1 and individual reflection survey

notes:
Checked 2026-10-10. Read all 197,423 characters / 2,208 lines of the markdown conversion, including Appendices A-G and appendix references. Quotations were extracted from the saved 118-page PDF with PyMuPDF; line breaks/whitespace were normalized, and otherwise source characters and footnote markers were retained. The saved version is INSEAD Working Paper 2026/17/STR dated 22 February 2026, revised from 2025/42/STR.

No public participant-level or output-level dataset was found for S1 or S2. The only matching external research record found is the public AEA preregistration, categorized here as materials_only. The paper's public PDF also supplies survey screenshots, prompts, the Rated case, coding rubrics, a keyword dictionary, aggregate tables and selected examples. The paper itself is not counted as a separate deposit.

The paper contains no participant-data sharing promise, data-repository URL, or analysis-code URL. The form's data_and_code.data_url and code_url are both empty. Appendix A's 'available upon request' statement refers only to other conditions' survey versions; it does not establish that data are available on request. The Rated case's proprietary-data statement concerns stimulus materials, not the participants' experimental responses.

Appendix C (PDF p. 72) specifies ResponseID, OptionID, Option, Strategic, Continue, Change Pricing of Ads, Exit and Note for a desired coding spreadsheet. These are printed instructions, not columns inspected in a released data file; rows_checked and columns_checked therefore remain null. Neither the described training/validation datasets nor interaction logs were publicly located.

Selected option examples (Table D.4), six illustrative participant prompts (Table E.2) and the 24 teams' input challenges (Table G.1) do not provide exhaustive scored outputs linked to participant assignments. Table G.1 lists input problems, not the teams' complete generated alternatives. They cannot support the requested per-person statistics or representative diversity measures. S2 outcome analysis is at the team level.

None of final.open_items can be resolved by computing statistics from publicly located data. In particular, the registry's 112/112/112 counts are planned allocations within the planned 336-person sample, not observed assignments among the paper's 338 assigned people. No released data dictionary resolves S2 Gender coding, and no released scores/texts/code resolve the scorer, word-count, significance or version-continuity questions.

Confidence is medium because SSRN and INSEAD landing pages returned HTTP 403 bot checks, so supplementary attachments behind those pages could not be inventoried, and repository searches cannot prove that an unindexed deposit does not exist. Public API searches and the public INSEAD PDF were available. Generic AEA 'Request Information' text is under Study Withdrawal; it is not evidence that an experimental dataset is available through approval. No account, login, contact, or access request was used.
